title: Project Tiger: From 9 Reserves

segments.say: In the early nineteen seventies, India's tigers were in trouble. A count found fewer than two thousand left.
In nineteen seventy-two came the Wild Life Protection Act. On the first of April, nineteen seventy-three, Project Tiger began, with nine tiger reserves.
Each reserve has a core, kept for the tiger, and a buffer around it, where people and the forest share the land.
In two thousand six, a law set up the National Tiger Conservation Authority to run the reserves, and a tiger count every four years.

The count was one thousand four hundred and eleven in two thousand six. By twenty twenty-two it was at least three thousand one hundred and sixty-seven. India now has about three-quarters of the world's wild tigers.
The hard part now is space. Tigers need corridors to move between forests, and those corridors are shrinking.
For Prelims: Project Tiger in nineteen seventy-three with nine reserves, the NTCA in two thousand six, and a count every four years.

sources: National Tiger Conservation Authority (ntca.gov.in): Project Tiger launched 1 April 1973 with 9 tiger reserves; core and buffer zones; NTCA constituted in 2006 under the amended Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972

NTCA / Wildlife Institute of India, 'Status of Tigers, Co-predators and Prey in India 2022' (released 2023): minimum 3,167 tigers by camera trap; earlier estimates 1,411 (2006), 2,226 (2014); India holds about 75% of the world's wild tigers
PIB, 9 April 2023: 50 years of Project Tiger; tiger census numbers

quiz.q: How many reserves did Project Tiger start with?
Which body runs tiger reserves today?
quiz.why: Set up in 2006 under the Wild Life (Protection) Act.
A minimum of 3,167 by camera trap.

reviewNote: Facts were read against NTCA's pages, the 2022 tiger status report and PIB (April 2023). Pictures show tigers only. Moving facts: the number of reserves keeps rising (not stated); the next census will change the counts.
